Card.description: Root of every rendered UI — children stack vertically inside one card in the chat. Keep it to two or three blocks: this sits in a narrow chat rail, under a message that has already done the explaining.

Text.description: A line or paragraph of prose. style: 'title' a small section heading · 'strong' emphasis · 'muted' a quiet aside · 'body' (default). Use ONE short Text to frame a decision — the chat message above already carries your explanation, so do not repeat it here.

Callout.description: A tinted banner for something the user must notice before choosing: a cost, an overwrite warning, a blocked prerequisite, a render that will take minutes. Use 'danger' only for destructive or irreversible consequences.

OptionList.description: THE default way to ask the author to choose — an inset card of Option rows separated by hairlines. Use it for 2–6 choices that need more than a bare label: models, durations, takes, drafts, characters to add, next steps. header: a small uppercase label above the card. footnote: one quiet line beneath it (e.g. 'Or just tell me what you want instead.'). select: 'one' (default) — a tap picks that item and sends immediately. 'many' — taps toggle and nothing is sent until the confirm button. 'one-per-group' — the items are split into sub-questions by their `group` prop, each group takes exactly ONE pick, and the confirm button unlocks only once every group is answered. Reach for 'many' whenever the author may legitimately want SEVERAL of the listed things (which speakers to add to the World, which takes to keep), and 'one-per-group' when you are asking the SAME question about several subjects at once (a voice per character, a length per scene). send: REQUIRED when select is 'many' or 'one-per-group': the lead of the composed message, to which the picked items' `send` values are appended after a colon — e.g. send "Add these characters to the World" + picks "Miles", "Vera" posts "Add these characters to the World: Miles, Vera". Ignored when select is 'one'. confirm: the confirm button's label when select is 'many' or 'one-per-group' (default "Continue"). Ignored when select is 'one'.

Option.description: One choice in an OptionList, rendered as a tappable row. title: the choice. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'. subtitle: one line of why-you'd-pick-this. meta: a short right-aligned qualifier ("~40s", "12 credits", "shot03"). image: a thumbnail URL for the row's leading badge. badge: a tiny pill ("Recommended", "Current"). selected: marks the option already in force. tone 'danger' for a destructive choice. group: ONLY for a list whose select is 'one-per-group': which sub-question this item answers, e.g. the character whose portrait this is ("Miles Okonkwo"). Items sharing a group are drawn together under it as a heading and are mutually exclusive. Groups appear in the order their first item does. Omit it in every other mode.

MediaGrid.description: A grid of image thumbnails. It does TWO jobs. (1) SHOWING finished pictures: the moment an image generation you started completes, draw this card with the result — that is how the author SEES it. Never answer an image job with prose alone ("it's on the Visual board", "saved to the library") and never paste the URL as markdown; the picture belongs in the chat, next to the words. Rows you are only showing get NO `send`, so there is no pick control under them. (2) ASKING which reference, still, take or character sheet to use — then each tile carries a `send`. Tapping a thumbnail always opens it FULL-SCREEN for a proper look; picking, when offered, is a separate explicit control so the author can inspect before committing. columns: 2 (default) or 3; use 3 only for six or more small thumbnails. A single image is fine — one tile, columns 2. select: 'one' (default) — a tap picks that item and sends immediately. 'many' — taps toggle and nothing is sent until the confirm button. 'one-per-group' — the items are split into sub-questions by their `group` prop, each group takes exactly ONE pick, and the confirm button unlocks only once every group is answered. Reach for 'many' when several images are legitimately wanted (a multi-reference generation), and 'one-per-group' for the very common CANDIDATES-PER-SUBJECT card: several portraits for each of several characters, several looks for each of several locations. One grid, one `group` per subject, one confirm. send: REQUIRED when select is 'many' or 'one-per-group': the lead of the composed message, to which the picked items' `send` values are appended after a colon — e.g. send "Add these characters to the World" + picks "Miles", "Vera" posts "Add these characters to the World: Miles, Vera". Ignored when select is 'one'. confirm: the confirm button's label when select is 'many' or 'one-per-group' (default "Continue"). Ignored when select is 'one'.

MediaItem.description: One image in a MediaGrid. src: the URL PAINTED ON THE TILE — pass the tool's `thumb` field whenever it has one (a ~400px webp of the same picture), so the card paints immediately instead of pulling a multi-megabyte original into the chat; fall back to the plain image URL only when there is no thumb. display: the URL OPENED FULL-SCREEN when the tile is tapped — pass the tool's `display` field (a ~1600px webp), so the author gets a sharp look without downloading the full original; OMIT it and the tile just re-opens `src`. (`thumb` and `display` are for LOOKING at — never pass either to a generation; that always takes the `refUrl`.) send: OPTIONAL — give it only when picking this image is a real decision; then it follows the usual rules (the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'; in a 'many' or 'one-per-group' grid a NOUN PHRASE instead, because the picks are joined into one sentence). OMIT send entirely when the card is just showing the author a picture you made — the tile is then look-only, with no "Use this" button under it. label: a short name under the thumbnail. caption: one extra line of context. selected: marks the current pick. group: ONLY for a list whose select is 'one-per-group': which sub-question this item answers, e.g. the character whose portrait this is ("Miles Okonkwo"). Items sharing a group are drawn together under it as a heading and are mutually exclusive. Groups appear in the order their first item does. Omit it in every other mode.

AudioList.description: A stack of playable audio rows — THE way to hand finished audio back to the author: a Seed Audio scene, radio takes, new sound versions. The author plays each clip right in the chat; NEVER paste an audio URL as a markdown link instead. Playing never sends anything — picking is a separate control that appears only on rows given a `send`, so a listen-only card is simply rows without one. select: 'one' (default) — a tap picks that item and sends immediately. 'many' — taps toggle and nothing is sent until the confirm button. 'one-per-group' — the items are split into sub-questions by their `group` prop, each group takes exactly ONE pick, and the confirm button unlocks only once every group is answered. Reach for 'many' when several takes can be kept, and 'one-per-group' to audition takes for several lines or characters in one card (group by the character or the line). send: REQUIRED when select is 'many' or 'one-per-group': the lead of the composed message, to which the picked items' `send` values are appended after a colon — e.g. send "Add these characters to the World" + picks "Miles", "Vera" posts "Add these characters to the World: Miles, Vera". Ignored when select is 'one'. confirm: the confirm button's label when select is 'many' or 'one-per-group' (default "Continue"). Ignored when select is 'one'.

AudioItem.description: One playable clip in an AudioList, rendered as a row with an inline play button. src: the audio URL (a /sound-media or generation URL a tool returned — never invent one). title: what the clip is ("Take 2 — heavier rain"). send: OPTIONAL — give it only when picking this clip is a real decision; then it follows the usual rules (the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'; in a 'many' or 'one-per-group' list a NOUN PHRASE instead). Omit send entirely when the card is just for listening. subtitle: one line of context (what changed in this take). meta: a short right-aligned qualifier ("12s", "v3"). badge: a tiny pill ("Liked", "New"). selected: marks the take already in force. group: ONLY for a list whose select is 'one-per-group': which sub-question this item answers, e.g. the character whose portrait this is ("Miles Okonkwo"). Items sharing a group are drawn together under it as a heading and are mutually exclusive. Groups appear in the order their first item does. Omit it in every other mode.

Recommendation.description: A single recommended course of action, presented as a hero card with one big call-to-action button. Use it when you have ONE thing to propose and want a clean yes — a render you're about to submit, a plan you'd run next, a draft you'd pin. title: the proposal. body: two sentences of why. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines' (the go-ahead). cta: the button text ("Render it", "Do it") — default "Continue". bullets: up to 4 short supporting facts. image: a preview thumbnail. meta: cost/duration ("~90s · 12 credits").

PluginList.description: THE way to answer a request that needs a capability this project has not installed. The answer is never "I can't" and never half the pipeline run with the parts you do have: show the plugin, say what it unlocks, and let one tap install it. Draw the plugin the work needs — or the two or three plausible ones — and then STOP, because the install is the author's call and nothing installs itself: their tap posts the message, and you call set_plugin on the turn after. NEVER more than three; a wall of plugins is a catalogue, not a decision. Do not draw a plugin that is already installed except to CONFIRM one is there (that is what Plugin's `installed` is for). When the missing plugin BLOCKS something they just asked for, put a Callout above it (variant 'info', or 'warning' when work is already part-done) so the reason is visible before the offer. header: a small uppercase label above the card. footnote: one quiet line beneath it ("You can always add it later from Explore plugins.").

Plugin.description: One plugin in a PluginList, drawn as a small marketplace card. name: what the marketplace calls it ("Radio", "Sound studio", "Shot list"). tagline: ONE line of what it does, in the author's terms — not a feature list. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'. For a plugin that opening is the install itself — the AUTHOR asking for it ("Install the Radio plugin"), never a report about them ("The user chose to install radio"). category: the shelf it sits on ("Story", "Visuals", "Audio", "Post"), drawn as a small eyebrow over the name. badge: a tiny pill saying why this one is on screen ("Needed for this", "Recommended"). meta: a short right-aligned qualifier. highlights: up to 4 short lines of WHAT THE AUTHOR GETS, not how it works. installed: true only for a plugin the project ALREADY has — it then renders settled, with no install control, so it is for CONFIRMING something is already there, never for offering it again.

Compare.description: Two or three options weighed side by side on identical rows — models, providers, takes, drafts. Use it only when the choice genuinely turns on comparing the SAME attributes; a plain OptionList reads better for everything else. Never more than 3 columns: the chat rail is narrow.

Column.description: One side of a Compare. label: what this column is ("Seedance", "Veo 3.1"). rows: the same {label, value} keys IN THE SAME ORDER as every other column, so they line up. badge: a tiny pill ("Recommended"). send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines' — supply it to make the whole column pickable.

KeyValue.description: A compact label/value detail block — the parameters of a render you're about to submit, a shot's settings, a cut's stats. Pair it with Actions to make a confirmation.

Steps.description: An ordered plan, numbered, shown BEFORE you run a multi-step pipeline so the author can see what's coming. steps: {title, detail?, meta?}. current: index of the step in progress (0-based) — omit when nothing has started yet.

Chips.description: A row of small follow-up pills. Tapping one sends its label verbatim as the user's next message, so write each as something the AUTHOR would say ('Show me the other takes'). Use for cheap side-quests offered alongside the main choice — never as the main choice itself.

Actions.description: A group of buttons — the plain yes/no/other choice. direction: 'row' (default) for two or three short labels, 'column' when the labels are sentences.

Action.description: One button. label: the button text. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'. Exactly ONE action in a group should be 'primary'. tone 'danger' for destructive or irreversible choices (overwrite, delete, regenerate over existing work).

Section.description: A titled group of blocks, separated from its neighbours by a rule. Only reach for it when one card genuinely carries two distinct groups (e.g. 'The references' and 'What I'd do'); a single-section card should skip it and put the blocks straight in the Card.
